description: Review, critique or roast any piece of marketing copy, whether it's an ad, a landing page, an email, a sales page, a social post or a script, and find out why it might not persuade. It takes the copy and line-by-line labels naming the reader question each persuasive line answers. It returns which of the nine questions the copy answers for its goal, which it answers weakly and which it skips, along with the biggest gap and what readers do when it is missing. It also checks the order, whether the answers agree with each other, and the craft, pointing to the exact words that read as machine-written, like em dashes, "it's not X, it's Y" lines and sentences that all run the same length. Then it checks the opening line and suggests techniques from the catalog to fill the gap. It answers requests like "is this good?", "roast this", "what's wrong with this copy?" and "how do I make it better?"

awareness_level.description: How much the reader already knows, on Eugene Schwartz's scale: unaware means they don't know they have the problem, problem_aware that they feel it, solution_aware that they know solutions exist, product_aware that they know you, and most_aware that they're ready and only need the offer.

brief.description: The brief, if you have it: the brand, product, offer, audience and proof. With it, the opening line gets the swap test, which asks whether a competitor could send it unchanged.

category.description: The industry, for a comparison with what brands in that category usually do. There is enough data for apparel, automotive, b2b_saas, beauty_skincare, business_coaching, consumer_tech, dtc_food_bev, dtc_health, fitness_health, home_goods, info_product, investing, marketing_education, otc_pharma, personal_care, personal_development, supplements, weight_loss. Any other category still works, just without the comparison.

copy.description: The full copy, exactly as written.

format.description: The kind of copy it is: ad, landing_page, sales_letter for long-form sales copy, email, email_subject, social_post, video_script or headline.

goal.description: What the copy has to get the reader to do: purchase means buy now, signup means an opt-in, a trial, a demo or a lead form, click means the whole job is the click (most ads and links), and engagement covers nurture emails, newsletters and social posts that should be read, answered or followed.

headline.description: The headline or opening line, if it isn't the first line of the copy.

moves.description: Line-by-line labels: each persuasive line quoted exactly, with the one reader question it mainly answers. Lines that are pure filler are left out.

clarity.description: clear: the line answers the question well. partial: it only gestures at it.

excerpt.description: An exact quote from the copy, whether a sentence, a line or a short passage.

question.description: The reader question the text answers, by its role name: DISRUPT for "Why am I even reading this?", IDENTIFY for "Is this written for me?", AGITATE for "How bad is my problem, really?", REFRAME for "Am I thinking about this correctly?", PROVE for "Can I trust the claim?", ELEVATE for "What does my life look like after?", RESOLVE for "What's stopping me from saying yes?", COMPEL for "Why should I act right now?", BOND for "Do I like and trust who's speaking?".

persuasion_mode.description: How hard the copy is allowed to push. Balanced is the default, persuasive and sustainable over time. Equity protects long-term trust, so it rules out fear, hype and hard-sell moves. Aggressive is for short-term direct response and allows fear, threat and hard scarcity. In every mode, the claims stay true.

title: Diagnose marketing copy (roast / review)
